I've now fully root-caused this, and it's deeper than a misconfigured repo — it's a real library ABI gap. Here's the definitive picture:

## Why it failed

| Layer | What's true on this box (Kali rolling 2026.2) |
|---|---|
| Repo written | Sury **`bookworm`** (Debian 12 *stable*) — `php.list` |
| Kali's libxml2 | **`libxml2-16` = libxml2 2.15.3**, ships only `libxml2.so.16`. The old `libxml2` package (`.so.2`) is **gone**, with no virtual `Provides`. |
| Kali's libzip | `libzip5` 1.11.4 (old `libzip4` gone) |
| Sury bookworm php8.5 needs | `libxml2 (≥2.9.4)` + `libzip4` → **both names absent on Kali** → the exact error you saw |
| Sury trixie php8.5 needs | `libzip5` ✅ (Kali has it) but **still `libxml2`** (`.so.2`) ❌ |
| Sury `forky`/`sid` suites | **Don't exist** (HTTP 418) |

Two distinct bugs in `apt_repository_manager.sh:132-138`:
1. **Kali maps to `bookworm`** (oldest) instead of the newest published Sury suite. `kali-rolling` isn't in the allowlist → falls back to `bookworm`.
2. The allowlist passes through `forky|sid`, but **Sury publishes neither** → those would 404/418.

**The unavoidable catch:** Kali (tracking Debian sid/forky) already moved to libxml2 2.15 / `.so.16`. Sury's newest build (trixie) still links `libxml2.so.2`. `php8.5-cli` itself depends on libxml2 (libxml is core, non-disableable PHP), so **no Sury PHP 8.5 can install *or run* on Kali 2026.2 without a `libxml2.so.2` present**. I verified the clean remedy: **Debian trixie's `libxml2` package (2.12.7, `.so.2`)** is co-installable — it depends only on `libc6`, `liblzma5`, `zlib1g`, all present on Kali, and won't collide with `libxml2-16` (different package name + different `.so` files).

So the fix has two parts: (A) **suite mapping** bookworm→trixie + clamp non-hosted codenames — unambiguously correct, I'll do it regardless; (B) **the libxml2 gap** — a judgment call on how aggressive to be.

Here's where things stand while the adversarial review finishes:

## Root cause (definitive)
Your `31_*.sh` → `apt_repository_manager.sh` mapped **Kali rolling → Sury `bookworm`** (Debian 12). But Kali 2026.2 tracks Debian sid and has moved past two SONAME transitions:
- `libxml2` → **`libxml2-16`** (libxml2 2.15.3, ships only `libxml2.so.16`; old `libxml2` package gone, no virtual `Provides`)
- `libzip4` → **`libzip5`**

Sury's bookworm php8.5 still `Depends: libxml2` + `libzip4` → neither exists on Kali → the exact `[no choices]` error. And `forky`/`sid` Sury suites **don't exist** (HTTP 418).

## Fix applied (in `apt_repository_manager.sh`)
1. **Suite mapping** — Debian codename clamp now keeps only `{bullseye,bookworm,trixie}` (the suites Sury/Docker/PGDG/Tailscale actually host); anything outside (kali‑rolling, parrot, forky, sid, empty) → **`trixie`** (newest hosted, matches Kali's post‑t64 ABi), env‑overridable via `APT_DEBIAN_CODENAME_DEFAULT`. trixie alone fixes the libzip side and the rest of the dep closure.
2. **libxml2 `.so.2` compat shim** (new `ensure_php_libxml2_compat_from_apt_repository_manager`) — the one remaining gap. When no `libxml2` satisfier exists, it pulls Debian trixie's real `libxml2` (2.12.7, `.so.2`; deps `libc6`/`liblzma5`/`zlib1g`, all present) and `dpkg -i`s it next to `libxml2-16`. Default‑on, opt out with `PHP_LIBXML2_COMPAT_SHIM=0`. Wired into both repo‑add functions, before the PHP install.

Empirically validated on your box: `bash -n` clean, resolver now emits `debian trixie`, the shim resolves the real `.deb` (HTTP 200), and the full php8.5 dep closure resolves on Kali with trixie **except** libxml2 (which the shim covers). 204	fix_file_permissions_from_apt_repository_manager() {
205	    local file_path="$1"
206	    local permissions="${2:-+x}"
207	    
208	    if [ -z "$file_path" ]; then
209	        return 1
210	    fi
211	    
212	    local real_user=$(get_real_login_user_from_apt_repository_manager)
213	    if [ -z "$real_user" ] || [ "$real_user" = "root" ]; then
214	        # If we can't determine real user, just chmod
215	        $USE_SUDO chmod "$permissions" "$file_path" 2>/dev/null || return 1
216	        return 0
217	    fi
218	    
219	    # Set ownership to real user first, then chmod
220	    $USE_SUDO chown "$real_user:$real_user" "$file_path" 2>/dev/null || true
221	    $USE_SUDO chmod "$permissions" "$file_path" 2>/dev/null || return 1
222

ensure_packages_from_apt_repository_manager() {
    local packages="$*"
    [ -z "$packages" ] && return 0
    
    local missing_packages=""
    for pkg in $packages; do
        if ! command -v "$pkg" >/dev/null 2>&1 && ! dpkg -l | grep -q "^ii.*$pkg "; then
            missing_packages="$missing_packages $pkg"
        fi
    done
    
    [ -z "$missing_packages" ] && return 0

## What happened on your last run
The first fix **worked** — PHP 8.5.7 installed and running, 9 extensions loaded, the libxml2 shim did its job (`OK: libxml2.so.2 now available`). The only remaining failure was the **same bug class, second instance**: `php8.5-intl` → `libicu76`. Kali bumped ICU past Sury-trixie's `libicu76`, exactly like it bumped libxml2 past `.so.2`.

## What I changed (so it's fixed generally, not whack-a-mole)
I **generalized** the one-off libxml2 shim in `apt_repository_manager.sh` into `ensure_php_compat_libs_from_apt_repository_manager`, which resolves **every** such SONAME gap in one pass, scoped to the project's actual php package set (`PHP85_CORE_PACKAGES` + `CORE_EXTENSIONS`):

1. Reads the Sury suite's `Depends` for the php packages you install → finds which `lib*` deps are unsatisfiable on this host. For Kali that's exactly `{libxml2, libicu76}` — and deliberately **not** `libsnmp40t64`/`libgpgme11t64` (those belong to extensions you don't install).
2. Pulls each from Debian trixie (the suite Sury built against → ABI match), co-installing next to Kali's newer versions.

I also folded in the adversarial review's findings:
- **Security:** `.deb`s now fetched over **HTTPS** and **SHA256-verified** against the Packages stanza before `dpkg -i` (was plain HTTP, no integrity check → root-RCE surface).
- **Robustness:** `DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive` + `--force-confold`, `apt-get -f install` constrained with `APT::Get::Remove=false` (can't remove the lib it just added), no swallowed diagnostics + loud post-verify, self-ensures curl/gzip, fatal-on-`mktemp` (no predictable temp path).
- **Cross-distro:** the bookworm→trixie default is now **glibc-gated** (a bookworm-era spin with glibc<2.38 stays on bookworm), and os-release reads are `set -u`-safe — so it correctly "supports Ubuntu / Debian / Kali."

- `bash -n` clean; resolver → `debian trixie`; opt-out (`PHP_COMPAT_SHIM=0`) works
- The detection pipeline run against the live indices yields **exactly `libicu76`** now (libxml2 excluded because it's installed → confirms idempotency), and parses the right `Filename` + SHA256 (`c1bf…`, HTTPS 200). On a fresh box it catches both libs and batches them.

## Summary — Swoole install (script 32) fixed for Ubuntu/Debian/Kali

**Two root causes, both fixed:**

**1. `/usr/tmp` Permission denied (the actual failure).** `GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR` was hardcoded to `/usr/tmp` — a legacy SysV alias for `/var/tmp` that exists only as a symlink on some RPM distros and is simply **absent on Debian/Kali**, so the clone got EACCES. Fixed in both `gvar_common.sh` and the `gvar_common.js` mirror:
- `GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR` now resolves to `${TMPDIR:-/var/tmp}` (writable, persistent, disk-backed — right for large source builds; world-writable+sticky on every Debian-family system). Confirmed → `/var/tmp`, writable.
- Only creates/chmods it when **missing** (never clobbers an existing temp dir's `1777` sticky bit), and the `create_script_temp_dir` guard now keys off `$GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR` instead of a hardcoded `/usr/tmp/*`.
- The swoole build now uses `mktemp -d` under it (no PID collisions).

**2. Wrong Swoole version (would fail/produce an unsupported binary on PHP 8.5).** The "v6.0.2 unavailable → master" message was a **misdiagnosis** — v6.0.2 *does* exist; the clone just failed on the path error. Per Swoole's **official `composer.json` `php` constraint**:

- `6.0.x` → predates PHP 8.5 · `6.1.x` → `>=8.1 **<8.5**` (**explicitly excludes 8.5**) · **`6.2.x` → `>=8.2 <8.6` (supports 8.5)**

So I added `select_swoole_build_ref`, which **selects an available, compatible version**: it takes the latest *stable* GitHub release, **validates its composer.json admits the running PHP**, and falls back to a known-good pin (`v6.2.1`) offline — honoring `SWOOLE_BUILD_REF` as an override. Tested live: it picks **`v6.2.1`** for PHP 8.5, and correctly rejects `v6.1.8`. Also replaced the misleading "fall back to master" with a real full-clone retry of the same ref + clear errors.

**Validated:** `bash -n` (both shell files), `node --check` (JS), helper logic against live Swoole data, and `/var/tmp` writability — all pass. The sudo-gated compile (`phpize`/`configure`/`make`) is the only part I can't run here; build deps (`php8.5-dev`, `build-essential`, `libssl-dev`, `libcurl4-openssl-dev`, `libpcre2-dev`) were already installed in your run.

**Action:** re-run `32_install_swoole.sh` — it'll build into `/var/tmp/swoole-src-build-XXXXXX` and clone **Swoole v6.2.1**.

## Why 31 and 32 weren't aligned (your question)

They **are** aligned in sourcing — both do `source …/gvar_common.sh` at line 33. The difference is purely functional:

- **31** is apt-only and **never touches `GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR`**, so the broken value was invisible to it.
- **32** builds Swoole **from source** and uses `GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR` as the build dir → it hit the bad value.

And the value was bad because of shared infra + runtime state:
1. The README bootstrap (`sudo mkdir -p /usr/tmp …`) / old gvar code physically **created `/usr/tmp` as `root:root 0755`** — unwritable by your user.
2. The long-running **menu exported `GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR=/usr/tmp`**, so every child inherits it.
3. My first fix used `${GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR:-…}`, which **preserved** that stale value, and since `/usr/tmp` now *exists*, the "create if missing" path was skipped.

Since the root cause is in shared infra, the fix belongs there — which is what truly aligns them.

## The fix
- **`gvar_common.sh`**: `GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR` now resolves to the **first *writable* candidate** — exported value → `$TMPDIR` → `/var/tmp` → `/tmp` — *skipping* a stale/unwritable inherited `/usr/tmp` instead of preserving it. Every script that uses it is now aligned and safe.
- **`32_install_swoole.sh`**: the build-dir `mktemp` also falls back through writable candidates, so it can never be blocked by a bad temp base again.

Net: **no menu restart needed** — on the next run, sourcing `gvar_common.sh` re-resolves `GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR` to `/var/tmp` inside the script.

## Action
Re-run `32_install_swoole.sh`. It'll build Swoole **v6.2.1** (already selected correctly last run) into `/var/tmp/swoole-src-build-XXXXXX`, then `phpize`/`configure`/`make`/`make install`.

Two optional follow-ups (say the word and I'll do them):
1. The leftover **`/usr/tmp` (root:root)** is now harmless but is clutter — `sudo rmdir /usr/tmp` if you want it gone.
2. The **README** install command still does `sudo mkdir -p /usr/tmp` (the origin of this whole thing) — I can switch the documented bootstrap to `/var/tmp` so fresh installs never recreate the unwritable dir.

[2026-06-22 21:43:23] ASSISTANT:
The downstream audit is running. Here's the answer to your question and what I've already fixed in **13** (the canonical source):

## Why `python` wasn't the venv (root cause)

`main()` calls **`fix_python_links` twice** — once *before* venv setup (line 18) and once *after* (line 23). `create_python_venv_and_replace_system` correctly sets `/usr/local/bin/python → venv` (line 704), but the **second `fix_python_links` immediately overwrites it back to `/usr/bin/python3` (system)** — because `fix_python_links` was hardcoded to target system python3. So the final `python` pointed at system, contradicting the design. Two more leaks compounded it:
- The DEPENDENCY_MAP installs ran via **system `python3 … --break-system-packages --no-user`**, not the venv.
- The venv was **`root:root`**, so even venv-pip printed *"site-packages not writeable"* and fell back to `~/.local`, then collided with dpkg/`/usr/local`.

## Fixes applied to 13 (validated: `bash -n` OK)
1. **`fix_python_links` is now venv-aware** → `python → $VENV_PYTHON3`, `pip → $VENV_PIP3` whenever the venv exists (so the before/after calls both yield the **venv** link instead of clobbering it). `python3`/`pip3` stay system, per your design.
2. **`check_and_fix_package_version` installs into the venv** (`$VENV_PYTHON3`) → `run_pip_install_realtime` then drops `--break-system-packages/--no-user` and packages land in the venv, not `~/.local`/`/usr/local`.
3. **`ensure_venv_user_writable`** repairs a stale `root`-owned venv back to the invoking user (it's created without sudo by design) — so pip writes *into* the venv. Runs before any venv pip op.
4. **AppIndicator** → picks `gir1.2-ayatanaappindicator3-0.1` (the Ayatana fork Kali/Debian/modern-Ubuntu ship), falls back to the old name, and the GUI batch now installs only packages with a real candidate so one missing name can't abort it.

Net: `python` = venv, installs go into the venv, venv is writable — the three things that have to agree for "calling `python` is calling the venv" to actually hold.

The rule applied everywhere, matching your existing `[NN]` convention:
- **Effectful** calls (installs, launches, `-m venv`) → print the command to stdout, then run.
- **Value-capturing** calls (`$(python3 -V)`, version/import probes) → print to **stderr** (`>&2`), so the command shows on the terminal but the captured value stays clean — the trap that would otherwise corrupt e.g. the resolved interpreter path or version string.

## Fixed — the migration fatal that blocked `start.sh`

**Root cause:** the 4 new `2026_06_21_*` migrations declared `protected string $connection;`, but Laravel's base `Illuminate\Database\Migrations\Migration` declares `$connection` **untyped** (`protected $connection;`). PHP property types are **invariant** across inheritance — a child may not add a type the parent doesn't have — so the class fatals at declaration: *"Type of …$connection must be omitted to match the parent definition."* It's a hard fatal on any modern PHP (you're on 8.5), independent of OS — so it's the same on WSL/Debian/Ubuntu/Kali.

**Fix:** dropped the type in all 4 so they match the parent (the constructor still assigns the connection name string — behavior unchanged):
```php
- protected string $connection;
+ protected $connection;
```
- `global_2026_06_21_100000_add_fast_lane_to_global_tasks.php`
- `global_2026_06_21_100001_add_capabilities_to_workers.php`
- `global_2026_06_21_100002_add_substrate_link_columns_to_global_tasks.php`
- `AppQyV1_2026_06_21_100003_add_global_task_id_to_dict_tables.php`

**Verified:** `php -l` clean; booted Laravel and **loaded + instantiated all 4 migration classes (constructors ran) with no fatal — 4/4**; and a repo-wide scan shows **no remaining** typed `$connection`/`$withinTransaction` shadowing the parent.

## Fixed — `node_modules` is updated in place, never wiped

**What was happening:** the `"… will be removed and reinstalled from scratch. Proceed?"` prompt is **pnpm's own** `ERR_PNPM_MODULES_BREAKING_CHANGE` — pnpm 11.8.0 found a `node_modules` created by an older pnpm major version and wanted to recreate it. The script's `ensure_deps` never ran `rm -rf`, but it forced `pnpm install` whenever the tree looked incomplete, which handed pnpm the chance to offer that wipe.

**New `ensure_deps` policy (matches "if node_modules exists, update — not remove and reinstall"):**

| Situation | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `node_modules` **exists** | `pnpm install --config.confirm-modules-purge=true < /dev/null` → **updates in place**; if pnpm deems it a breaking change it **errors instead of wiping**, and the script **keeps** the tree (+warns) |
| `node_modules` missing/empty | normal fresh `pnpm install` |
| `--force-install` | explicit from-scratch reinstall (purge allowed, non-interactive) |

The key mechanism: running pnpm **non-interactively** with `confirm-modules-purge` at its default (`true`) means pnpm will **never purge unprompted** — on a breaking change it aborts rather than destroying `node_modules`. So you keep your modules and just get an incremental update; a clean recreate is now an explicit opt-in (`--force-install`).

Trade-off you asked for: if an existing `node_modules` is genuinely broken (e.g., `vite` missing) the in-place update may error and keep it — the script warns and continues instead of wiping; pass `--force-install` when you actually want a clean rebuild.

The matching **`start.ps1`** (Windows) still has the old logic — say the word and I'll mirror this same in-place-update policy there for sh/ps1 parity.

# COMMON REPOSITORY MANAGEMENT FUNCTIONS
# ============================================================================

# Bridge the libxml2 SONAME gap so Sury PHP 8.5 can install AND run on bleeding-edge
# Debian derivatives (e.g. Kali rolling).
#
# Sury's php8.5-cli / php8.5-xml depend on the historic `libxml2` package, which
# ships libxml2.so.2. Rolling derivativ already moved to
# libxml2 2.15 (package `libxml2-16`, soname libxml2.so.16) and dropped the old
# `libxml2` package with no virtual Pro unsatisfiable
# and, even if force-installed, the PHP binary (linked against .so.2) would fail to
# load. libxml2 is core, non-disableable PHP, so this blocks PHP entirely.
#
# When the gap is detected, install Debian's `libxml2` (.so.2) compat package for the
# resolved Sury codename (the suite Sury built against, so the ABI matches). It depends
# only on libc6/liblzma5/zlib1g (present on such systems) and co-installs cleanly next
# to libxml2-16 (different package name, different .so files). Idempotent; a no-op when
# libxml2.so.2 is already present or the distro still ships a real `libxml2` candidate.
#
# Opt out with PHP_LIBXML2_COMPAT_SHIM=0 -- then a clear gap message is printed and the
# caller's PHP install is left to fail loudly instead of silently mixing in a lib.
ensure_php_libxml2_compat_from_apt_repository_manager() {
    local php_vendor="$1"     # ubuntu | debian
    local php_codename="$2"   # resolved repo codename (e.g. trixie)

    # Only the Debian/Sury path is affected; Ubuntu's ondrej PPA tracks Ubuntu libs.
    [ "$php_vendor" = "debian" ] || return 0

    # Already satisfiable? Either the distro offers a real `libxml2` candidate, the
    # .so.2 is already on disk (prior sge is installed.
    local cand
    cand="$(apt-cache policy libxml2 2>/dev/null | awk '/Candidate:/{print $2}')"
    if [ -n "$cand" ] && [ "$cand" != "(none)" ]; then
        return 0
    fi
    if ldconfig -p 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'libxml2\.so\.2'; then
        return 0
    fi
    if dpkg-query -W -f='${Status}' libxml2 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'install ok installed'; then
        return 0
    fi

    echo "[libxml2-compat] This distro has no 'libxml2' (libxml2.so.2) package that Sury PHP 8.5 needs;" >&2
    echo "[libxml2-compat]   it ships only the newer libxml2-16 / libxml2.so.16." >&2

    case "${PHP_LIBXML2_COMPAT_SHIM:-1}" in
        0|false|no|off)
            echo "[libxml2-compat] PHP_-> NOT installing the compat lib." >&2
            echo "[libxml2-compat] The PHP 8.5 install will fail until libxml2.so.2 is provided." >&2
            echo "[libxml2-compat] Re-rIM=1 (default) to auto-install it." >&2
            return 0
            ;;
    esac

    local arch; arch="$(dpkg --print-architecture 2>/dev/null || echo amd64)"
    local idx_url="http://deb.debian.org/debian/dists/${php_codename}/main/binary-${arch}/Packages.gz"
    echo "[libxml2-compat] Resolving Debian ${php_codename} libxml2 (.so.2) compat package..." >&2

    local tmp; tmp="$(mktemp -d 2>/dev/null || echo "/tmp/libxml2compat.$$")"
    mkdir -p "$tmp"
    local idx="$tmp/Packages.gz"
    if ! curl -fsSL -o "$idx" "$idx_url"; then
        echo "[libxml2-compat] ERROR: could not fetch Debian package index ($idx_url)." >&2
        rm -rf "$tmp"; return 1
    fi

    # Filename: of the binary package named exactly 'libxml2' (the .so.2 one). The
    # trailing \n in the regex preventsxml2-dev / etc.
    local fname
    fname="$(zcat "$idx" 2>/dev/null \
        | awk 'BEGIN{RS="";ORS="\n\n"} /(^|\n)Package: libxml2\n/' \
        | sed -n 's/^Filename: //p' | head -n1)"
    if [ -z "$fname" ]; then
        echo "[libxml2-compat] ERROR: Debian ${php_codename} has no 'libxml2' (.so.2) package." >&2
        rm -rf "$tmp"; return 1
    fi

    local deb_url="http://deb.debian.org/debian/${fname}"
    local deb="$tmp/libxml2-compat.deb"
    echo "[libxml2-compat] Downloading ${deb_url}" >&2
    if ! curl -fsSL -o "$deb" "$deb_url"; then
        echo "[libxml2-compat] ERROR: download failed ($deb_url)." >&2
        rm -rf "$tmp"; return 1
    fi

    echo "[libxml2-compat] Installing compat libxml2 (.so.2) alongside libxml2-16..." >&2
    if ! $USE_SUDO dpkg -i "$deb"; then
        # Pull any missing deps from th1g normally present).
        $USE_SUDO apt-get -f install -y 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
    rm -rf "$tmp"

    if ldconfig -p 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'libxml2\.so\.2'; then
        echo "[libxml2-compat] OK: libxml2.so.2 now available (Debian ${php_codename} compat lib)." >&2
        return 0
    fi
    echo "[libxml2-compat] WARNING: libxml2.so.2 still absent after shim; PHP install may fail." >&2
    return 1
}

# Add PHP repository (Ubuntu/Debian) with automatic backup and restore
# Ubuntu: uses ppa.launchpadcontent.net and Launchpad PPA signing key (avoids certificate mismatch with ppa.lau
nchpad.net)
# Debian: uses packages.sury.org and Sury key

# COMMON REPOSITORY MANAGEMENT FUNCTIONS
# ============================================================================

# Bridge the libxml2 SONAME gap so Sury PHP 8.5 can install AND run on bleeding-edge
# Debian derivatives (e.g. Kali rolling).
# Bridge SONAME/library gaps so Sury PHbleeding-edge
# Debian derivatives (e.g. Kali rolling) that have moved ahead of the suite Sury
# builds against.
#
# Sury's php8.5-cli / php8.5-xml depend on the historic `libxml2` package, which
# ships libxml2.so.2. Rolling derivatives that track Debian sid have already moved to
# libxml2 2.15 (package `libxml2-16`, soname libxml2.so.16) and dropped the old
# `libxml2` package with no virtual Provides -- so the dependency is unsatisfiable
# and, even if force-installed, the PHP binary (linked against .so.2) would fail to
# load. libxml2 is core, non-disableable PHP, so this blocks PHP entirely.
# Sury's php8.5-* packages (built for Debian <codename>) depend on that suite's library
# versions -- e.g. php8.5-cli/xml -> `libxml2` (libxml2.so.2), php8.5-intl -> `libicu76`.
# Rolling derivatives that track Debian sid have already bumped those SONAMEs (libxml2
# 2.15 -> package libxml2-16 / libxml2.so.16; ICU 76 -> libicu77+) and DROPPED the old
# package names with no virtual Provides, so the dependency is unsatisfiable and the
# extension binaries (linked against the old soname) would not load. libxml2 is core,
# non-disableable PHP, so a missing libxml2 blocks PHP entirely.
#
# When the gap is detected, install Debian's `libxml2` (.so.2) compat package for the
# resolved Sury codename (the suite Sury built against, so the ABI matches). It depends
# only on libc6/liblzma5/zlib1g (presentalls cleanly next
# to libxml2-16 (different package name, different .so files). Idempotent; a no-op when
# libxml2.so.2 is already present or thlibxml2` candidate.
# For each library dependency of the REQUESTED php packages that is unsatisfiable on
# this host, install Debian <codename>'s build of that exact library (the suite Sury
# built against -> ABI match). Such libs are SONAME-versioned, so they co-install
# cleanly next to the distro's newer version (different package name + different .so).
# Only libs that the requested php packages actually need AND that the host lacks AND
# that Debian publishes are touched -- never a blanket pull (so e.g. libsnmp40t64 for
# php8.5-snmp is left alone when that extension is not requested). Idempotent: a no-op
# once the libs are installed or the distro already satisfies them.
#
# Opt out with PHP_LIBXML2_COMPAT_SHIM=0 -- then a clear gap message is printed and the
# caller's PHP install is left to fail loudly instead of silently mixing in a lib.
ensure_php_libxml2_compat_from_apt_repository_manager() {
    local php_vendor="$1"     # ubuntu | debian
    local php_codename="$2"   # resolved repo codename (e.g. trixie)
# Security: each .deb is fetched over HTTPS and verified against the SHA256 in the same
# Packages index stanza before it is installed as root; a mismatch discards the file.
#
# Opt out with PHP_COMPAT_SHIM=0 (legacIM=0) -- then a
# clear gap report is printed and the caller's PHP install is left to fail loudly
# instead of silently mixing in a lib.
#
# Args: <vendor: ubuntu|debian> <codename> <space-separated php package list>
ensure_php_compat_libs_from_apt_repository_manager() {
    local php_vendor="$1"
    local php_codename="$2"
    local php_pkgs="$3"

    # Only the Debian/Sury path is affected; Ubuntu's ondrej PPA tracks Ubuntu libs.
    [ "$php_vendor" = "debian" ] || return 0
    [ -n "${php_pkgs// /}" ] || return 0

    # Already satisfiable? Either the distro offers a real `libxml2` candidate, the
    # .so.2 is already on disk (prior shim / leftover), or the package is installed.
    local cand
    cand="$(apt-cache policy libxml2 2>/dev/null | awk '/Candidate:/{print $2}')"
    if [ -n "$cand" ] && [ "$cand" != "(none)" ]; then
        return 0
    fi
    if ldconfig -p 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'libxml2\.so\.2'; then
        return 0
    fi
    if dpkg-query -W -f='${Status}' libxml2 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'install ok installed'; then
        return 0
    fi

    echo "[libxml2-compat] This distro has no 'libxml2' (libxml2.so.2) package that Sury PHP 8.5 needs;" >&2
    echo "[libxml2-compat]   it ships only the newer libxml2-16 / libxml2.so.16." >&2

    case "${PHP_LIBXML2_COMPAT_SHIM:-1}" in
    case "${PHP_COMPAT_SHIM:-${PHP_LIBXML2_COMPAT_SHIM:-1}}" in
        0|false|no|off)
            echo "[libxml2-compat] PHP_LIBXML2_COMPAT_SHIM disabled -> NOT installing the compat lib." >&2
            echo "[libxml2-compat] The PHP 8.5 install will fail until libxml2.so.2 is provided." >&2
            echo "[libxml2-compat] Re-run with PHP_LIBXML2_COMPAT_SHIM=1 (default) to auto-install it." >&2
            echo "[php-compat] Compat-lib shim disabled (PHP_COMPAT_SHIM=0); not adjusting libraries." >&2
            echo "[php-compat] If Sury PHP 8.5 deps are unsatisfiable on this distro, the install will fail." >
&2
            return 0
            ;;
    esac

    # Be self-contained regardless of caller order (the shim fetches/unpacks on its own).
    command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1 || ensure_packages_from_apt_repository_manager curl 2>/dev/null || true
    command -v zcat >/dev/null 2>&1 || ensure_packages_from_apt_repository_manager gzip 2>/dev/null || true

    local arch; arch="$(dpkg --print-architecture 2>/dev/null || echo amd64)"
    local idx_url="http://deb.debian.org/debian/dists/${php_codename}/main/binary-${arch}/Packages.gz"
    echo "[libxml2-compat] Resolving Debian ${php_codename} libxml2 (.so.2) compat package..." >&2
    local tmp
    tmp="$(mktemp -d 2>/dev/null)" || {
        echo "[php-compat] ERROR: mktemp -d failed; refusing a predictable temp path." >&2
        return 1
    }

    local tmp; tmp="$(mktemp -d 2>/dev/null || echo "/tmp/libxml2compat.$$")"
    mkdir -p "$tmp"
    local idx="$tmp/Packages.gz"
    if ! curl -fsSL -o "$idx" "$idx_url
        echo "[libxml2-compat] ERROR: could not fetch Debian package index ($idx_url)." >&2
        rm -rf "$tmp"; return 1
    # 1) Sury index for the resolved suite -> the php8.5-* dependency lists.
    local sury_idx="$tmp/sury.Packages.gz"
    if ! curl -fsSL -o "$sury_idx" "https://packages.sury.org/php/dists/${php_codename}/main/binary-${arch}/Pac
kages.gz"; then
        echo "[php-compat] WARNING: could not fetch Sury ${php_codename} index; skipping compat pre-resolution.
" >&2
        rm -rf "$tmp"; return 0
    fi

    # Filename: of the binary package named exactly 'libxml2' (the .so.2 one). The
    # trailing \n in the regex prevents matching libxml2-utils / libxml2-dev / etc.
    local fname
    fname="$(zcat "$idx" 2>/dev/null \
        | awk 'BEGIN{RS="";ORS="\n\n"} /(^|\n)Package: libxml2\n/' \
        | sed -n 's/^Filename: //p' | head -n1)"
    if [ -z "$fname" ]; then
        echo "[libxml2-compat] ERROR: Debian ${php_codename} has no 'libxml2' (.so.2) package." >&2
        rm -rf "$tmp"; return 1
    # 2) Union of the lib* deps of the requested php packages (strip version constraints
    #    and '|' alternatives). index()l -> no regex pitfalls.
    local pkg
    for pkg in $php_pkgs; do
        zcat "$sury_idx" 2>/dev/null \
          | awk -v RS='' -v p="$pkg" 'index($0 "\n", "Package: " p "\n")==1' \
          | sed -n 's/^Depends: //p'
    done > "$tmp/depends.txt" 2>/dev/null
    local libs
    libs="$(tr ',' '\n' < "$tmp/depends.txt" | sed 's/|.*//; s/^[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]].*//' | grep -E '^
lib' | sort -u)"

    # 3) Which of those lib deps are UNsatisfiable on this host?
    local gaps="" lib cand
    for lib in $libs; do
        cand="$(apt-cache policy "$lib" 2>/dev/null | awk '/Candidate:/{print $2}')"
        if [ -n "$cand" ] && [ "$cand" != "(none)" ]; then continue; fi
        if dpkg-query -W -f='${Status}' "$lib" 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'install ok installed'; then continue; fi
        gaps="$gaps $lib"
    done
    gaps="$(printf '%s\n' $gaps | sed '/^$/d' | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ')"

    if [ -z "${gaps// /}" ]; then
        rm -rf "$tmp"; return 0
    fi

    local deb_url="http://deb.debian.org/debian/${fname}"
    local deb="$tmp/libxml2-compat.deb"
    echo "[libxml2-compat] Downloading ${deb_url}" >&2
    if ! curl -fsSL -o "$deb" "$deb_url"; then
        echo "[libxml2-compat] ERROR: download failed ($deb_url)." >&2
    echo "[php-compat] Sury PHP 8.5 needs libraries this distro no longer provides:${gaps}" >&2
    echo "[php-compat] (a rolling derivative bumped these SONAMEs past Sury's ${php_codename} build target)" >&
2

    # 4) Resolve + integrity-verify each gap lib from Debian <codename> (the suite Sury
    #    built against), then collect the verified .debs.
    local deb_idx="$tmp/debian.Packages.gz"
    if ! curl -fsSL -o "$deb_idx" "https://deb.debian.org/debian/dists/${php_codename}/main/binary-${arch}/Pack
ages.gz"; then
        echo "[php-compat] ERROR: could not fetch Debian ${php_codename} index; cannot provide compat libs." >&
2
        rm -rf "$tmp"; return 1
    fi

    echo "[libxml2-compat] Installing compat libxml2 (.so.2) alongside libxml2-16..." >&2
    if ! $USE_SUDO dpkg -i "$deb"; then
        # Pull any missing deps from the distro (libc6/liblzma5/zlib1g normally present).
        $USE_SUDO apt-get -f install -y 2>/dev/null || true
    local debs="" missing="" stanza fname exp_sha got_sha out
    for lib in $gaps; do
        stanza="$(zcat "$deb_idx" 2>/dev/null | awk -v RS='' -v p="$lib" 'index($0 "\n", "Package: " p "\n")==1
' | head -c 200000)"
        fname="$(printf '%s\n' "$stanza" | sed -n 's/^Filename: //p' | head -n1)"
        exp_sha="$(printf '%s\n' "$stanza" | sed -n 's/^SHA256: //p' | head -n1)"
        if [ -z "$fname" ]; then
            echo "[php-compat] NOTE: Debian ${php_codename} has no '${lib}' package; cannot shim it." >&2
            missing="$missing $lib"; continue
        fi
        out="$tmp/${lib}.deb"
        echo "[php-compat] Fetching ${lib} <- https://deb.debian.org/debian/${fname}" >&2
        if ! curl -fsSL -o "$out" "httpname}"; then
            echo "[php-compat] WARNING: download failed for ${lib}." >&2
            missing="$missing $lib"; continue
        fi
        if [ -z "$exp_sha" ]; then
            echo "[php-compat] ERROR: no SHA256 in index for ${lib}; refusing to install unverified .deb." >&2
            missing="$missing $lib"; continue
        fi
        got_sha="$(sha256sum "$out" 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}')"
        if [ "$got_sha" != "$exp_sha" ]; then
            echo "[php-compat] ERROR: SHA256 mismatch for ${lib} (want ${exp_sha}, got ${got_sha}); discarding.
" >&2
            missing="$missing $lib"; continue
        fi
        debs="$debs $out"
    done

    # 5) Install all verified compat libs at once (so any inter-deps resolve together),
    #    non-interactively, keeping exioving packages to
    #    "fix" the transaction. Diagnostics are NOT swallowed.
    if [ -n "${debs// /}" ]; then
        echo "[php-compat] Installing verified compat libs alongside the distro's newer versions..." >&2
        if ! $USE_SUDO env DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive dpkg -i --force-confold $debs; then
            $USE_SUDO env DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -f install -y \
                -o APT::Get::Remove=false -o Dpkg::Options::=--force-confold || true
        fi
    fi

    # 6) Verify outcome loudly. A lib that is unshimmable (no Debian package / failed
    #    verify) is reported but not treated as the whole step failing.
    local still_missing=""
    for lib in $gaps; do
        if dpkg-query -W -f='${Status}' "$lib" 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'install ok installed'; then continue; fi
        case " $missing " in *" $lib "*) continue ;; esac
        still_missing="$still_missing $lib"
    done

    rm -rf "$tmp"

    if ldconfig -p 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'libxml2\.so\.2'; then
        echo "[libxml2-compat] OK: libxn ${php_codename} compat lib)." >&2
        return 0
    if [ -n "${still_missing// /}" ]; then
        echo "[php-compat] WARNING: compat libs still not installed:${still_missing} -- the PHP packages needin
g them will fail." >&2
        return 1
    fi
    echo "[libxml2-compat] WARNING: libxml2.so.2 still absent after shim; PHP install may fail." >&2
    return 1
    if [ -n "${missing// /}" ]; then
        echo "[php-compat] NOTE: no verified Debian compat for:${missing} (only extensions needing them are aff
ected)." >&2
    fi
    echo "[php-compat] OK: compat libraries provided for ${php_codename}." >&2
    return 0
}

    fi
}

# Does a given Swoole git ref's official composer.json `php` constraint admit the running
# PHP? Returns 0 (yes / undeterminable) or 1 (explicitly excluded). Parses the simple
# ">=X.Y" + optional "<A.B" forms Swoole uses (e.g. ">=8.2 <8.6", ">=8.1 <8.5").
swoole_ref_supports_php() {
    local ref="$1" php_ver="$2"
    local pvid; pvid="$(echo "$php_ver"100+$2}')"
    local constraint
    constraint="$(curl -fsSL "https://rle/swoole-src/${ref}/composer.json" 2>/dev/
null \
        | sed -n 's/.*"php"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -n1)"
    [ -z "$constraint" ] && return 0   # offline / unknown -> do not block
    local lo hi
    lo="$(printf '%s' "$constraint" | grep -oE '>=?[[:space:]]*[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -n1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[
0-9]+')"
    hi="$(printf '%s' "$constraint" | grep -oE '<[[:space:]]*[0-9]+\.[0-9]+'   | head -n1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[
0-9]+')"
    if [ -n "$lo" ]; then
        local loid; loid="$(echo "$lo" | awk -F. '{printf "%d", $1*100+$2}')"
        [ "$pvid" -lt "$loid" ] && return 1
    fi
    if [ -n "$hi" ]; then
        local hiid; hiid="$(echo "$hi" | awk -F. '{printf "%d", $1*100+$2}')"
        [ "$pvid" -ge "$hiid" ] && return 1
    fi
    return 0
}

# Select the Swoole build ref for the rlable version" rather
# than trust a possibly-stale hardcoded tag:
#   1. $SWOOLE_BUILD_REF if set (explicit override).
#   2. the latest STABLE GitHub release, IF its composer.json admits this PHP.
#   3. the provided known-good pin, IF it admits this PHP.
#   4. master (last resort), with a warning.
# Prints the chosen ref on stdout (diagnostics go to stderr).
select_swoole_build_ref() {
    local php_ver="$1" pin="$2"
    if [ -n "${SWOOLE_BUILD_REF:-}" ]; then
        echo "$SWOOLE_BUILD_REF"; return 0
    fi
    local latest
    latest="$(curl -fsSL "https://api.github.com/repos/swoole/swoole-src/releases/latest" 2>/dev/null \
        | sed -n 's/.*"tag_name"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -n1)"
    if printf '%s' "$latest" | grep -qE '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' && swoole_ref_supports_php "$latest" "$php_
ver"; then
        echo "$latest"; return 0
    fi
    if swoole_ref_supports_php "$pin" "$php_ver"; then
        echo "$pin"; return 0
    fi
    echo "[WARN] No tagged Swoole release admits PHP ${php_ver}; falling back to master" >&2
    echo "master"
}

# Initialize global temporary directory.
# NOTE: /usr/tmp is a legacy SysV alias for /var/tmp that exists only as a symlink on
# some RPM distros; on Debian/Ubuntu/Kali it is absent, so clones/builds under it failed
# with "Permission denied". Use $TMPDIR when set, else /var/tmp -- persistent and
# disk-backed (good for large source builds, unlike RAM-backed /tmp) and world-writable
# + sticky on every Debian-family system, so the invoking non-root user can create build
# dirs here. Export GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR to override.
GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR="${GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR:-${TMPDIR:-/var/tmp}}"
GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR="${GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR%/}"
# Initialize the global temporary directory base.
# It MUST be writable by the invoking (non-root) user, because scripts clone/build here
# as the user (then `make install` as root). Pitfalls this resolver defends against:
#   * /usr/tmp is a legacy SysV alias n/Ubuntu/Kali; worse,
#     an older revision of this file created it as root:root 0755 (unwritable), and a
#     long-running menu may still EXPOnto child scripts.
#   * So a stale/unwritable INHERITED value must be SKIPPED, not preserved -- using
#     "${GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR:-...}" alone would keep the bad /usr/tmp.
# Resolution order (first that is a WRITABLE dir, or can be created writable, wins):
#   exported GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR, $TMPDIR, /var/tmp, /tmp. /var/tmp is preferred (persistent +
#   disk-backed -> good for large source builds, unlike RAM-backed /tmp).
__resolve_global_temp_dir_from_gvar_common() {
    local c
    for c in "${GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR:-}" "${TMPDIR:-}" /var/tmp /tmp; do
        [ -z "$c" ] && continue
        c="${c%/}"
        if { [ -d "$c" ] || mkdir -p "$c" 2>/dev/null; } && [ -w "$c" ]; then
            echo "$c"; return 0
        fi
    done
    echo /tmp
}
GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR="$(__resolve_global_temp_dir_from_gvar_common)"
unset -f __resolve_global_temp_dir_fro

# Ensure global temporary directory exMISSING -- never
# chmod an existing system temp dir, which would clobber its 1777 sticky permissions.
if [ ! -d "$GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR" ]; then
    echo "Creating global temporary directory: $GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR"
    mkdir -p "$GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR" 2>/dev/null || $USE_SUDO mkdir -p "$GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR"
    chmod 1777 "$GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR" 2>/dev/null || $USE_SUDO chmod 1777 "$GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR" 2>/dev/null || true
fi

# Function to create script-specific temporary directory (restricted to $GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR/<script_name>)
create_script_temp_dir() {
    local script_name="$1"

ensure_php_symlink() {
    echo -e "${BLUE}$SCRIPT_INDEX Ensuring PHP 8.5 symlink exists...${NC}"
    echo -e "${BLUE}$SCRIPT_INDEX Ensuring PHP ${PHP_VERSION} is the default php...${NC}"

    if [ ! -f "/usr/bin/php" ] || ! /usr/bin/php -v 2>/dev/null | grep -q "PHP 8.5"; then
        echo -e "${YELLOW}$SCRIPT_INDEX PHP 8.5 symlink missing or incorrect, fixing...${NC}"
    if [ ! -x "$PHP_BIN" ]; then
        echo -e "${RED}$SCRIPT_INDEX PHP ${PHP_VERSION} binary not found at $PHP_BIN${NC}"
        echo -e "${YELLOW}$SCRIPT_INDEX Please run 31_ensure_php85_intelligent.sh first${NC}"
        return 1
    fi

        if [ -f "/usr/bin/php8.5" ]; then
            # Register php8.5 (idempotent) without wiping other PHP alternatives.
            # --remove-all would destroy every registered php alternative on rerun.
            $USE_SUDO update-alternativ /usr/bin/php8.5 84
            $USE_SUDO update-alternatives --set php /usr/bin/php8.5
            echo -e "${GREEN}$SCRIPT_INC}"
        else
            echo -e "${RED}$SCRIPT_INDEX PHP 8.5 binary not found at /usr/bin/php8.5${NC}"
            echo -e "${YELLOW}$SCRIPT_INDEX Please run 31_ensure_php84_intelligent.sh first${NC}"
            return 1
        fi
    else
        echo -e "${GREEN}$SCRIPT_INDEX PHP 8.5 symlink already exists${NC}"
    # 1) /usr/bin/php via update-alternatives -- SAME priority as step 31 (shared
    #    PHP_ALT_PRIORITY) so re-running this step never lowers the default 31 set.
    #    No --remove-all (that would wipe other registered php alternatives).
    if [ ! -e "/usr/bin/php" ] || ! /usr/bin/php -v 2>/dev/null | grep -q "PHP ${PHP_VERSION}"; then
        $USE_SUDO update-alternatives --install /usr/bin/php php "$PHP_BIN" "$PHP_ALT_PRIORITY"
        $USE_SUDO update-alternatives --set php "$PHP_BIN"
        echo -e "${GREEN}$SCRIPT_INDEX PHP ${PHP_VERSION} set as default (priority ${PHP_ALT_PRIORITY})${NC}"
    fi

    if /usr/bin/php -v 2>/dev/null | grep -q "PHP 8.5"; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}$SCRIPT_INDEX r/bin/php${NC}"
    # 2) The canonical entrypoint link that step 31 CREATES and step 34 CONSUMES.
    #    32 previously only checked /ushile this contract
    #    link was broken. Keep it in sync here too.
    if [ "$(readlink -f "$TARGET_LINK_PATH" 2>/dev/null)" != "$(readlink -f "$PHP_BIN" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
        $USE_SUDO mkdir -p "$(dirname "$TARGET_LINK_PATH")"
        $USE_SUDO ln -sf "$PHP_BIN" "$TARGET_LINK_PATH"
        echo -e "${GREEN}$SCRIPT_INDEX Linked $TARGET_LINK_PATH -> $PHP_BIN${NC}"
    fi

    if "$TARGET_LINK_PATH" -v 2>/dev/null | grep -q "PHP ${PHP_VERSION}"; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}$SCRIPT_INDEX PHP ${PHP_VERSION} available at $TARGET_LINK_PATH and /usr/bin/php${NC}"
        return 0
    else
        echo -e "${RED}$SCRIPT_INDEX Failed to set PHP 8.5 as default${NC}"
        echo -e "${RED}$SCRIPT_INDEX Failed to make PHP ${PHP_VERSION} the default${NC}"
        return 1
    fi
}

● Update(/mnt/dev_nvme0n1p1/programing/core_node/scripts/shells/linux/common/apt_repository_manager.sh)

# COMMON REPOSITORY MANAGEMENT FUNCTIONS
# ============================================================================

# Bridge the libxml2 SONAME gap so Sury PHP 8.5 can install AND run on bleeding-edge
# Debian derivatives (e.g. Kali rolling).
#
# Sury's php8.5-cli / php8.5-xml depend on the historic `libxml2` package, which
# ships libxml2.so.2. Rolling derivativ already moved to
# libxml2 2.15 (package `libxml2-16`, soname libxml2.so.16) and dropped the old
# `libxml2` package with no virtual Pro unsatisfiable
# and, even if force-installed, the PHP binary (linked against .so.2) would fail to
# load. libxml2 is core, non-disableable PHP, so this blocks PHP entirely.
#
# When the gap is detected, install Debian's `libxml2` (.so.2) compat package for the
# resolved Sury codename (the suite Sury built against, so the ABI matches). It depends
# only on libc6/liblzma5/zlib1g (present on such systems) and co-installs cleanly next
# to libxml2-16 (different package name, different .so files). Idempotent; a no-op when
# libxml2.so.2 is already present or the distro still ships a real `libxml2` candidate.
#
# Opt out with PHP_LIBXML2_COMPAT_SHIM=0 -- then a clear gap message is printed and the
# caller's PHP install is left to fail loudly instead of silently mixing in a lib.
ensure_php_libxml2_compat_from_apt_repository_manager() {
    local php_vendor="$1"     # ubuntu | debian
    local php_codename="$2"   # resolved repo codename (e.g. trixie)

    # Only the Debian/Sury path is affected; Ubuntu's ondrej PPA tracks Ubuntu libs.
    [ "$php_vendor" = "debian" ] || return 0

    # Already satisfiable? Either the distro offers a real `libxml2` candidate, the
    # .so.2 is already on disk (prior sge is installed.
    local cand
    cand="$(apt-cache policy libxml2 2>/dev/null | awk '/Candidate:/{print $2}')"
    if [ -n "$cand" ] && [ "$cand" != "(none)" ]; then
        return 0
    fi
    if ldconfig -p 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'libxml2\.so\.2'; then
        return 0
    fi
    if dpkg-query -W -f='${Status}' libxml2 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'install ok installed'; then
        return 0
    fi

    echo "[libxml2-compat] This distro has no 'libxml2' (libxml2.so.2) package that Sury PHP 8.5 needs;" >&2
    echo "[libxml2-compat]   it ships only the newer libxml2-16 / libxml2.so.16." >&2

    case "${PHP_LIBXML2_COMPAT_SHIM:-1}" in
        0|false|no|off)
            echo "[libxml2-compat] PHP_-> NOT installing the compat lib." >&2
            echo "[libxml2-compat] The PHP 8.5 install will fail until libxml2.so.2 is provided." >&2
            echo "[libxml2-compat] Re-rIM=1 (default) to auto-install it." >&2
            return 0
            ;;
    esac

    local arch; arch="$(dpkg --print-architecture 2>/dev/null || echo amd64)"
    local idx_url="http://deb.debian.org/debian/dists/${php_codename}/main/binary-${arch}/Packages.gz"
    echo "[libxml2-compat] Resolving Debian ${php_codename} libxml2 (.so.2) compat package..." >&2

    local tmp; tmp="$(mktemp -d 2>/dev/null || echo "/tmp/libxml2compat.$$")"
    mkdir -p "$tmp"
    local idx="$tmp/Packages.gz"
    if ! curl -fsSL -o "$idx" "$idx_url"; then
        echo "[libxml2-compat] ERROR: could not fetch Debian package index ($idx_url)." >&2
        rm -rf "$tmp"; return 1
    fi

    # Filename: of the binary package named exactly 'libxml2' (the .so.2 one). The
    # trailing \n in the regex preventsxml2-dev / etc.
    local fname
    fname="$(zcat "$idx" 2>/dev/null \
        | awk 'BEGIN{RS="";ORS="\n\n"} /(^|\n)Package: libxml2\n/' \
        | sed -n 's/^Filename: //p' | head -n1)"
    if [ -z "$fname" ]; then
        echo "[libxml2-compat] ERROR: Debian ${php_codename} has no 'libxml2' (.so.2) package." >&2
        rm -rf "$tmp"; return 1
    fi

    local deb_url="http://deb.debian.org/debian/${fname}"
    local deb="$tmp/libxml2-compat.deb"
    echo "[libxml2-compat] Downloading ${deb_url}" >&2
    if ! curl -fsSL -o "$deb" "$deb_url"; then
        echo "[libxml2-compat] ERROR: download failed ($deb_url)." >&2
        rm -rf "$tmp"; return 1
    fi

    echo "[libxml2-compat] Installing compat libxml2 (.so.2) alongside libxml2-16..." >&2
    if ! $USE_SUDO dpkg -i "$deb"; then
        # Pull any missing deps from th1g normally present).
        $USE_SUDO apt-get -f install -y 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
    rm -rf "$tmp"

    if ldconfig -p 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'libxml2\.so\.2'; then
        echo "[libxml2-compat] OK: libxml2.so.2 now available (Debian ${php_codename} compat lib)." >&2
        return 0
    fi
    echo "[libxml2-compat] WARNING: libxml2.so.2 still absent after shim; PHP install may fail." >&2
    return 1
}

# Add PHP repository (Ubuntu/Debian) with automatic backup and restore
# Ubuntu: uses ppa.launchpadcontent.net and Launchpad PPA signing key (avoids certificate mismatch with ppa.lau
nchpad.net)
# Debian: uses packages.sury.org and Sury key

# COMMON REPOSITORY MANAGEMENT FUNCTIONS
# ============================================================================

# Bridge the libxml2 SONAME gap so Sury PHP 8.5 can install AND run on bleeding-edge
# Debian derivatives (e.g. Kali rolling).
# Bridge SONAME/library gaps so Sury PHbleeding-edge
# Debian derivatives (e.g. Kali rolling) that have moved ahead of the suite Sury
# builds against.
#
# Sury's php8.5-cli / php8.5-xml depend on the historic `libxml2` package, which
# ships libxml2.so.2. Rolling derivatives that track Debian sid have already moved to
# libxml2 2.15 (package `libxml2-16`, soname libxml2.so.16) and dropped the old
# `libxml2` package with no virtual Provides -- so the dependency is unsatisfiable
# and, even if force-installed, the PHP binary (linked against .so.2) would fail to
# load. libxml2 is core, non-disableable PHP, so this blocks PHP entirely.
# Sury's php8.5-* packages (built for Debian <codename>) depend on that suite's library
# versions -- e.g. php8.5-cli/xml -> `libxml2` (libxml2.so.2), php8.5-intl -> `libicu76`.
# Rolling derivatives that track Debian sid have already bumped those SONAMEs (libxml2
# 2.15 -> package libxml2-16 / libxml2.so.16; ICU 76 -> libicu77+) and DROPPED the old
# package names with no virtual Provides, so the dependency is unsatisfiable and the
# extension binaries (linked against the old soname) would not load. libxml2 is core,
# non-disableable PHP, so a missing libxml2 blocks PHP entirely.
#
# When the gap is detected, install Debian's `libxml2` (.so.2) compat package for the
# resolved Sury codename (the suite Sury built against, so the ABI matches). It depends
# only on libc6/liblzma5/zlib1g (presentalls cleanly next
# to libxml2-16 (different package name, different .so files). Idempotent; a no-op when
# libxml2.so.2 is already present or thlibxml2` candidate.
# For each library dependency of the REQUESTED php packages that is unsatisfiable on
# this host, install Debian <codename>'s build of that exact library (the suite Sury
# built against -> ABI match). Such libs are SONAME-versioned, so they co-install
# cleanly next to the distro's newer version (different package name + different .so).
# Only libs that the requested php packages actually need AND that the host lacks AND
# that Debian publishes are touched -- never a blanket pull (so e.g. libsnmp40t64 for
# php8.5-snmp is left alone when that extension is not requested). Idempotent: a no-op
# once the libs are installed or the distro already satisfies them.
#
# Opt out with PHP_LIBXML2_COMPAT_SHIM=0 -- then a clear gap message is printed and the
# caller's PHP install is left to fail loudly instead of silently mixing in a lib.
ensure_php_libxml2_compat_from_apt_repository_manager() {
    local php_vendor="$1"     # ubuntu | debian
    local php_codename="$2"   # resolved repo codename (e.g. trixie)
# Security: each .deb is fetched over HTTPS and verified against the SHA256 in the same
# Packages index stanza before it is installed as root; a mismatch discards the file.
#
# Opt out with PHP_COMPAT_SHIM=0 (legacIM=0) -- then a
# clear gap report is printed and the caller's PHP install is left to fail loudly
# instead of silently mixing in a lib.
#
# Args: <vendor: ubuntu|debian> <codename> <space-separated php package list>
ensure_php_compat_libs_from_apt_repository_manager() {
    local php_vendor="$1"
    local php_codename="$2"
    local php_pkgs="$3"

    # Only the Debian/Sury path is affected; Ubuntu's ondrej PPA tracks Ubuntu libs.
    [ "$php_vendor" = "debian" ] || return 0
    [ -n "${php_pkgs// /}" ] || return 0

    # Already satisfiable? Either the distro offers a real `libxml2` candidate, the
    # .so.2 is already on disk (prior shim / leftover), or the package is installed.
    local cand
    cand="$(apt-cache policy libxml2 2>/dev/null | awk '/Candidate:/{print $2}')"
    if [ -n "$cand" ] && [ "$cand" != "(none)" ]; then
        return 0
    fi
    if ldconfig -p 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'libxml2\.so\.2'; then
        return 0
    fi
    if dpkg-query -W -f='${Status}' libxml2 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'install ok installed'; then
        return 0
    fi

    echo "[libxml2-compat] This distro has no 'libxml2' (libxml2.so.2) package that Sury PHP 8.5 needs;" >&2
    echo "[libxml2-compat]   it ships only the newer libxml2-16 / libxml2.so.16." >&2

    case "${PHP_LIBXML2_COMPAT_SHIM:-1}" in
    case "${PHP_COMPAT_SHIM:-${PHP_LIBXML2_COMPAT_SHIM:-1}}" in
        0|false|no|off)
            echo "[libxml2-compat] PHP_LIBXML2_COMPAT_SHIM disabled -> NOT installing the compat lib." >&2
            echo "[libxml2-compat] The PHP 8.5 install will fail until libxml2.so.2 is provided." >&2
            echo "[libxml2-compat] Re-run with PHP_LIBXML2_COMPAT_SHIM=1 (default) to auto-install it." >&2
            echo "[php-compat] Compat-lib shim disabled (PHP_COMPAT_SHIM=0); not adjusting libraries." >&2
            echo "[php-compat] If Sury PHP 8.5 deps are unsatisfiable on this distro, the install will fail." >
&2
            return 0
            ;;
    esac

    # Be self-contained regardless of caller order (the shim fetches/unpacks on its own).
    command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1 || ensure_packages_from_apt_repository_manager curl 2>/dev/null || true
    command -v zcat >/dev/null 2>&1 || ensure_packages_from_apt_repository_manager gzip 2>/dev/null || true

    local arch; arch="$(dpkg --print-architecture 2>/dev/null || echo amd64)"
    local idx_url="http://deb.debian.org/debian/dists/${php_codename}/main/binary-${arch}/Packages.gz"
    echo "[libxml2-compat] Resolving Debian ${php_codename} libxml2 (.so.2) compat package..." >&2
    local tmp
    tmp="$(mktemp -d 2>/dev/null)" || {
        echo "[php-compat] ERROR: mktemp -d failed; refusing a predictable temp path." >&2
        return 1
    }

    local tmp; tmp="$(mktemp -d 2>/dev/null || echo "/tmp/libxml2compat.$$")"
    mkdir -p "$tmp"
    local idx="$tmp/Packages.gz"
    if ! curl -fsSL -o "$idx" "$idx_url
        echo "[libxml2-compat] ERROR: could not fetch Debian package index ($idx_url)." >&2
        rm -rf "$tmp"; return 1
    # 1) Sury index for the resolved suite -> the php8.5-* dependency lists.
    local sury_idx="$tmp/sury.Packages.gz"
    if ! curl -fsSL -o "$sury_idx" "https://packages.sury.org/php/dists/${php_codename}/main/binary-${arch}/Pac
kages.gz"; then
        echo "[php-compat] WARNING: could not fetch Sury ${php_codename} index; skipping compat pre-resolution.
" >&2
        rm -rf "$tmp"; return 0
    fi

    # Filename: of the binary package named exactly 'libxml2' (the .so.2 one). The
    # trailing \n in the regex prevents matching libxml2-utils / libxml2-dev / etc.
    local fname
    fname="$(zcat "$idx" 2>/dev/null \
        | awk 'BEGIN{RS="";ORS="\n\n"} /(^|\n)Package: libxml2\n/' \
        | sed -n 's/^Filename: //p' | head -n1)"
    if [ -z "$fname" ]; then
        echo "[libxml2-compat] ERROR: Debian ${php_codename} has no 'libxml2' (.so.2) package." >&2
        rm -rf "$tmp"; return 1
    # 2) Union of the lib* deps of the requested php packages (strip version constraints
    #    and '|' alternatives). index()l -> no regex pitfalls.
    local pkg
    for pkg in $php_pkgs; do
        zcat "$sury_idx" 2>/dev/null \
          | awk -v RS='' -v p="$pkg" 'index($0 "\n", "Package: " p "\n")==1' \
          | sed -n 's/^Depends: //p'
    done > "$tmp/depends.txt" 2>/dev/null
    local libs
    libs="$(tr ',' '\n' < "$tmp/depends.txt" | sed 's/|.*//; s/^[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]].*//' | grep -E '^
lib' | sort -u)"

    # 3) Which of those lib deps are UNsatisfiable on this host?
    local gaps="" lib cand
    for lib in $libs; do
        cand="$(apt-cache policy "$lib" 2>/dev/null | awk '/Candidate:/{print $2}')"
        if [ -n "$cand" ] && [ "$cand" != "(none)" ]; then continue; fi
        if dpkg-query -W -f='${Status}' "$lib" 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'install ok installed'; then continue; fi
        gaps="$gaps $lib"
    done
    gaps="$(printf '%s\n' $gaps | sed '/^$/d' | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ')"

    if [ -z "${gaps// /}" ]; then
        rm -rf "$tmp"; return 0
    fi

    local deb_url="http://deb.debian.org/debian/${fname}"
    local deb="$tmp/libxml2-compat.deb"
    echo "[libxml2-compat] Downloading ${deb_url}" >&2
    if ! curl -fsSL -o "$deb" "$deb_url"; then
        echo "[libxml2-compat] ERROR: download failed ($deb_url)." >&2
    echo "[php-compat] Sury PHP 8.5 needs libraries this distro no longer provides:${gaps}" >&2
    echo "[php-compat] (a rolling derivative bumped these SONAMEs past Sury's ${php_codename} build target)" >&
2

    # 4) Resolve + integrity-verify each gap lib from Debian <codename> (the suite Sury
    #    built against), then collect the verified .debs.
    local deb_idx="$tmp/debian.Packages.gz"
    if ! curl -fsSL -o "$deb_idx" "https://deb.debian.org/debian/dists/${php_codename}/main/binary-${arch}/Pack
ages.gz"; then
        echo "[php-compat] ERROR: could not fetch Debian ${php_codename} index; cannot provide compat libs." >&
2
        rm -rf "$tmp"; return 1
    fi

    echo "[libxml2-compat] Installing compat libxml2 (.so.2) alongside libxml2-16..." >&2
    if ! $USE_SUDO dpkg -i "$deb"; then
        # Pull any missing deps from the distro (libc6/liblzma5/zlib1g normally present).
        $USE_SUDO apt-get -f install -y 2>/dev/null || true
    local debs="" missing="" stanza fname exp_sha got_sha out
    for lib in $gaps; do
        stanza="$(zcat "$deb_idx" 2>/dev/null | awk -v RS='' -v p="$lib" 'index($0 "\n", "Package: " p "\n")==1
' | head -c 200000)"
        fname="$(printf '%s\n' "$stanza" | sed -n 's/^Filename: //p' | head -n1)"
        exp_sha="$(printf '%s\n' "$stanza" | sed -n 's/^SHA256: //p' | head -n1)"
        if [ -z "$fname" ]; then
            echo "[php-compat] NOTE: Debian ${php_codename} has no '${lib}' package; cannot shim it." >&2
            missing="$missing $lib"; continue
        fi
        out="$tmp/${lib}.deb"
        echo "[php-compat] Fetching ${lib} <- https://deb.debian.org/debian/${fname}" >&2
        if ! curl -fsSL -o "$out" "httpname}"; then
            echo "[php-compat] WARNING: download failed for ${lib}." >&2
            missing="$missing $lib"; continue
        fi
        if [ -z "$exp_sha" ]; then
            echo "[php-compat] ERROR: no SHA256 in index for ${lib}; refusing to install unverified .deb." >&2
            missing="$missing $lib"; continue
        fi
        got_sha="$(sha256sum "$out" 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}')"
        if [ "$got_sha" != "$exp_sha" ]; then
            echo "[php-compat] ERROR: SHA256 mismatch for ${lib} (want ${exp_sha}, got ${got_sha}); discarding.
" >&2
            missing="$missing $lib"; continue
        fi
        debs="$debs $out"
    done

    # 5) Install all verified compat libs at once (so any inter-deps resolve together),
    #    non-interactively, keeping exioving packages to
    #    "fix" the transaction. Diagnostics are NOT swallowed.
    if [ -n "${debs// /}" ]; then
        echo "[php-compat] Installing verified compat libs alongside the distro's newer versions..." >&2
        if ! $USE_SUDO env DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive dpkg -i --force-confold $debs; then
            $USE_SUDO env DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -f install -y \
                -o APT::Get::Remove=false -o Dpkg::Options::=--force-confold || true
        fi
    fi

    # 6) Verify outcome loudly. A lib that is unshimmable (no Debian package / failed
    #    verify) is reported but not treated as the whole step failing.
    local still_missing=""
    for lib in $gaps; do
        if dpkg-query -W -f='${Status}' "$lib" 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'install ok installed'; then continue; fi
        case " $missing " in *" $lib "*) continue ;; esac
        still_missing="$still_missing $lib"
    done

    rm -rf "$tmp"

    if ldconfig -p 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'libxml2\.so\.2'; then
        echo "[libxml2-compat] OK: libxn ${php_codename} compat lib)." >&2
        return 0
    if [ -n "${still_missing// /}" ]; then
        echo "[php-compat] WARNING: compat libs still not installed:${still_missing} -- the PHP packages needin
g them will fail." >&2
        return 1
    fi
    echo "[libxml2-compat] WARNING: libxml2.so.2 still absent after shim; PHP install may fail." >&2
    return 1
    if [ -n "${missing// /}" ]; then
        echo "[php-compat] NOTE: no verified Debian compat for:${missing} (only extensions needing them are aff
ected)." >&2
    fi
    echo "[php-compat] OK: compat libraries provided for ${php_codename}." >&2
    return 0
}

# some RPM distros; on Debian/Ubuntu/Kuilds under it failed
# with "Permission denied". Use $TMPDIR when set, else /var/tmp -- persistent and

# Does a given Swoole git ref's official composer.json `php` constraint admit the running
# PHP? Returns 0 (yes / undeterminable) or 1 (explicitly excluded). Parses the simple
# ">=X.Y" + optional "<A.B" forms Swoole uses (e.g. ">=8.2 <8.6", ">=8.1 <8.5").
swoole_ref_supports_php() {
    local ref="$1" php_ver="$2"
    local pvid; pvid="$(echo "$php_ver"100+$2}')"
    local constraint
    constraint="$(curl -fsSL "https://rle/swoole-src/${ref}/composer.json" 2>/dev/
null \
        | sed -n 's/.*"php"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -n1)"
    [ -z "$constraint" ] && return 0   # offline / unknown -> do not block
    local lo hi
    lo="$(printf '%s' "$constraint" | grep -oE '>=?[[:space:]]*[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -n1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[
0-9]+')"
    hi="$(printf '%s' "$constraint" | grep -oE '<[[:space:]]*[0-9]+\.[0-9]+'   | head -n1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[
0-9]+')"
    if [ -n "$lo" ]; then
        local loid; loid="$(echo "$lo" | awk -F. '{printf "%d", $1*100+$2}')"
        [ "$pvid" -lt "$loid" ] && return 1
    fi
    if [ -n "$hi" ]; then
        local hiid; hiid="$(echo "$hi" | awk -F. '{printf "%d", $1*100+$2}')"
        [ "$pvid" -ge "$hiid" ] && return 1
    fi
    return 0
}

# Select the Swoole build ref for the rlable version" rather
# than trust a possibly-stale hardcoded tag:
#   1. $SWOOLE_BUILD_REF if set (explicit override).
#   2. the latest STABLE GitHub release, IF its composer.json admits this PHP.
#   3. the provided known-good pin, IF it admits this PHP.
#   4. master (last resort), with a warning.
# Prints the chosen ref on stdout (diagnostics go to stderr).
select_swoole_build_ref() {
    local php_ver="$1" pin="$2"
    if [ -n "${SWOOLE_BUILD_REF:-}" ]; then
        echo "$SWOOLE_BUILD_REF"; return 0
    fi
    local latest
    latest="$(curl -fsSL "https://api.github.com/repos/swoole/swoole-src/releases/latest" 2>/dev/null \
        | sed -n 's/.*"tag_name"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -n1)"
    if printf '%s' "$latest" | grep -qE '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' && swoole_ref_supports_php "$latest" "$php_
ver"; then
        echo "$latest"; return 0
    fi
    if swoole_ref_supports_php "$pin" "$php_ver"; then
        echo "$pin"; return 0
    fi
    echo "[WARN] No tagged Swoole release admits PHP ${php_ver}; falling back to master" >&2
    echo "master"
}

# Initialize global temporary directory.
# NOTE: /usr/tmp is a legacy SysV alias for /var/tmp that exists only as a symlink on
# some RPM distros; on Debian/Ubuntu/Kali it is absent, so clones/builds under it failed
# with "Permission denied". Use $TMPDIR when set, else /var/tmp -- persistent and
# disk-backed (good for large source builds, unlike RAM-backed /tmp) and world-writable
# + sticky on every Debian-family system, so the invoking non-root user can create build
# dirs here. Export GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR to override.
GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR="${GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR:-${TMPDIR:-/var/tmp}}"
GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR="${GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR%/}"
# Initialize the global temporary directory base.
# It MUST be writable by the invoking (non-root) user, because scripts clone/build here
# as the user (then `make install` as root). Pitfalls this resolver defends against:
#   * /usr/tmp is a legacy SysV alias n/Ubuntu/Kali; worse,
#     an older revision of this file created it as root:root 0755 (unwritable), and a
#     long-running menu may still EXPOnto child scripts.
#   * So a stale/unwritable INHERITED value must be SKIPPED, not preserved -- using
#     "${GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR:-...}" alone would keep the bad /usr/tmp.
# Resolution order (first that is a WRITABLE dir, or can be created writable, wins):
#   exported GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR, $TMPDIR, /var/tmp, /tmp. /var/tmp is preferred (persistent +
#   disk-backed -> good for large source builds, unlike RAM-backed /tmp).
__resolve_global_temp_dir_from_gvar_common() {
    local c
    for c in "${GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR:-}" "${TMPDIR:-}" /var/tmp /tmp; do
        [ -z "$c" ] && continue
        c="${c%/}"
        if { [ -d "$c" ] || mkdir -p "$c" 2>/dev/null; } && [ -w "$c" ]; then
            echo "$c"; return 0
        fi
    done
    echo /tmp
}
GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR="$(__resolve_global_temp_dir_from_gvar_common)"
unset -f __resolve_global_temp_dir_fro

# Ensure global temporary directory exMISSING -- never
# chmod an existing system temp dir, which would clobber its 1777 sticky permissions.
if [ ! -d "$GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR" ]; then
    echo "Creating global temporary directory: $GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR"
    mkdir -p "$GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR" 2>/dev/null || $USE_SUDO mkdir -p "$GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR"
    chmod 1777 "$GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR" 2>/dev/null || $USE_SUDO chmod 1777 "$GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR" 2>/dev/null || true
fi

# Function to create script-specific temporary directory (restricted to $GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR/<script_name>)
create_script_temp_dir() {
    local script_name="$1"

ensure_php_symlink() {
    echo -e "${BLUE}$SCRIPT_INDEX Ensuring PHP 8.5 symlink exists...${NC}"
    echo -e "${BLUE}$SCRIPT_INDEX Ensuring PHP ${PHP_VERSION} is the default php...${NC}"

    if [ ! -f "/usr/bin/php" ] || ! /usr/bin/php -v 2>/dev/null | grep -q "PHP 8.5"; then
        echo -e "${YELLOW}$SCRIPT_INDEX PHP 8.5 symlink missing or incorrect, fixing...${NC}"
    if [ ! -x "$PHP_BIN" ]; then
        echo -e "${RED}$SCRIPT_INDEX PHP ${PHP_VERSION} binary not found at $PHP_BIN${NC}"
        echo -e "${YELLOW}$SCRIPT_INDEX Please run 31_ensure_php85_intelligent.sh first${NC}"
        return 1
    fi

        if [ -f "/usr/bin/php8.5" ]; then
            # Register php8.5 (idempotent) without wiping other PHP alternatives.
            # --remove-all would destroy every registered php alternative on rerun.
            $USE_SUDO update-alternativ /usr/bin/php8.5 84
            $USE_SUDO update-alternatives --set php /usr/bin/php8.5
            echo -e "${GREEN}$SCRIPT_INC}"
        else
            echo -e "${RED}$SCRIPT_INDEX PHP 8.5 binary not found at /usr/bin/php8.5${NC}"
            echo -e "${YELLOW}$SCRIPT_INDEX Please run 31_ensure_php84_intelligent.sh first${NC}"
            return 1
        fi
    else
        echo -e "${GREEN}$SCRIPT_INDEX PHP 8.5 symlink already exists${NC}"
    # 1) /usr/bin/php via update-alternatives -- SAME priority as step 31 (shared
    #    PHP_ALT_PRIORITY) so re-running this step never lowers the default 31 set.
    #    No --remove-all (that would wipe other registered php alternatives).
    if [ ! -e "/usr/bin/php" ] || ! /usr/bin/php -v 2>/dev/null | grep -q "PHP ${PHP_VERSION}"; then
        $USE_SUDO update-alternatives --install /usr/bin/php php "$PHP_BIN" "$PHP_ALT_PRIORITY"
        $USE_SUDO update-alternatives --set php "$PHP_BIN"
        echo -e "${GREEN}$SCRIPT_INDEX PHP ${PHP_VERSION} set as default (priority ${PHP_ALT_PRIORITY})${NC}"
    fi

    if /usr/bin/php -v 2>/dev/null | grep -q "PHP 8.5"; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}$SCRIPT_INDEX r/bin/php${NC}"
    # 2) The canonical entrypoint link that step 31 CREATES and step 34 CONSUMES.
    #    32 previously only checked /ushile this contract
    #    link was broken. Keep it in sync here too.
    if [ "$(readlink -f "$TARGET_LINK_PATH" 2>/dev/null)" != "$(readlink -f "$PHP_BIN" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
        $USE_SUDO mkdir -p "$(dirname "$TARGET_LINK_PATH")"
        $USE_SUDO ln -sf "$PHP_BIN" "$TARGET_LINK_PATH"
        echo -e "${GREEN}$SCRIPT_INDEX Linked $TARGET_LINK_PATH -> $PHP_BIN${NC}"
    fi

    if "$TARGET_LINK_PATH" -v 2>/dev/null | grep -q "PHP ${PHP_VERSION}"; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}$SCRIPT_INDEX PHP ${PHP_VERSION} available at $TARGET_LINK_PATH and /usr/bin/php${NC}"
        return 0
    else
        echo -e "${RED}$SCRIPT_INDEX Failed to set PHP 8.5 as default${NC}"
        echo -e "${RED}$SCRIPT_INDEX Failed to make PHP ${PHP_VERSION} the default${NC}"
        return 1
    fi
}

● Update(/mnt/dev_nvme0n1p1/programing/core_node/scripts/shells/linux/common/apt_repository_manager.sh)

# COMMON REPOSITORY MANAGEMENT FUNCTIONS
# ============================================================================

# Bridge the libxml2 SONAME gap so Sury PHP 8.5 can install AND run on bleeding-edge
# Debian derivatives (e.g. Kali rolling).
#
# Sury's php8.5-cli / php8.5-xml depend on the historic `libxml2` package, which
# ships libxml2.so.2. Rolling derivativ already moved to
# libxml2 2.15 (package `libxml2-16`, soname libxml2.so.16) and dropped the old
# `libxml2` package with no virtual Pro unsatisfiable
# and, even if force-installed, the PHP binary (linked against .so.2) would fail to
# load. libxml2 is core, non-disableable PHP, so this blocks PHP entirely.
#
# When the gap is detected, install Debian's `libxml2` (.so.2) compat package for the
# resolved Sury codename (the suite Sury built against, so the ABI matches). It depends
# only on libc6/liblzma5/zlib1g (present on such systems) and co-installs cleanly next
# to libxml2-16 (different package name, different .so files). Idempotent; a no-op when
# libxml2.so.2 is already present or the distro still ships a real `libxml2` candidate.
#
# Opt out with PHP_LIBXML2_COMPAT_SHIM=0 -- then a clear gap message is printed and the
# caller's PHP install is left to fail loudly instead of silently mixing in a lib.
ensure_php_libxml2_compat_from_apt_repository_manager() {
    local php_vendor="$1"     # ubuntu | debian
    local php_codename="$2"   # resolved repo codename (e.g. trixie)

    # Only the Debian/Sury path is affected; Ubuntu's ondrej PPA tracks Ubuntu libs.
    [ "$php_vendor" = "debian" ] || return 0

    # Already satisfiable? Either the distro offers a real `libxml2` candidate, the
    # .so.2 is already on disk (prior sge is installed.
    local cand
    cand="$(apt-cache policy libxml2 2>/dev/null | awk '/Candidate:/{print $2}')"
    if [ -n "$cand" ] && [ "$cand" != "(none)" ]; then
        return 0
    fi
    if ldconfig -p 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'libxml2\.so\.2'; then
        return 0
    fi
    if dpkg-query -W -f='${Status}' libxml2 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'install ok installed'; then
        return 0
    fi

    echo "[libxml2-compat] This distro has no 'libxml2' (libxml2.so.2) package that Sury PHP 8.5 needs;" >&2
    echo "[libxml2-compat]   it ships only the newer libxml2-16 / libxml2.so.16." >&2

    case "${PHP_LIBXML2_COMPAT_SHIM:-1}" in
        0|false|no|off)
            echo "[libxml2-compat] PHP_-> NOT installing the compat lib." >&2
            echo "[libxml2-compat] The PHP 8.5 install will fail until libxml2.so.2 is provided." >&2
            echo "[libxml2-compat] Re-rIM=1 (default) to auto-install it." >&2
            return 0
            ;;
    esac

    local arch; arch="$(dpkg --print-architecture 2>/dev/null || echo amd64)"
    local idx_url="http://deb.debian.org/debian/dists/${php_codename}/main/binary-${arch}/Packages.gz"
    echo "[libxml2-compat] Resolving Debian ${php_codename} libxml2 (.so.2) compat package..." >&2

    local tmp; tmp="$(mktemp -d 2>/dev/null || echo "/tmp/libxml2compat.$$")"
    mkdir -p "$tmp"
    local idx="$tmp/Packages.gz"
    if ! curl -fsSL -o "$idx" "$idx_url"; then
        echo "[libxml2-compat] ERROR: could not fetch Debian package index ($idx_url)." >&2
        rm -rf "$tmp"; return 1
    fi

    # Filename: of the binary package named exactly 'libxml2' (the .so.2 one). The
    # trailing \n in the regex preventsxml2-dev / etc.
    local fname
    fname="$(zcat "$idx" 2>/dev/null \
        | awk 'BEGIN{RS="";ORS="\n\n"} /(^|\n)Package: libxml2\n/' \
        | sed -n 's/^Filename: //p' | head -n1)"
    if [ -z "$fname" ]; then
        echo "[libxml2-compat] ERROR: Debian ${php_codename} has no 'libxml2' (.so.2) package." >&2
        rm -rf "$tmp"; return 1
    fi

    local deb_url="http://deb.debian.org/debian/${fname}"
    local deb="$tmp/libxml2-compat.deb"
    echo "[libxml2-compat] Downloading ${deb_url}" >&2
    if ! curl -fsSL -o "$deb" "$deb_url"; then
        echo "[libxml2-compat] ERROR: download failed ($deb_url)." >&2
        rm -rf "$tmp"; return 1
    fi

    echo "[libxml2-compat] Installing compat libxml2 (.so.2) alongside libxml2-16..." >&2
    if ! $USE_SUDO dpkg -i "$deb"; then
        # Pull any missing deps from th1g normally present).
        $USE_SUDO apt-get -f install -y 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
    rm -rf "$tmp"

    if ldconfig -p 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'libxml2\.so\.2'; then
        echo "[libxml2-compat] OK: libxml2.so.2 now available (Debian ${php_codename} compat lib)." >&2
        return 0
    fi
    echo "[libxml2-compat] WARNING: libxml2.so.2 still absent after shim; PHP install may fail." >&2
    return 1
}

# Add PHP repository (Ubuntu/Debian) with automatic backup and restore
# Ubuntu: uses ppa.launchpadcontent.net and Launchpad PPA signing key (avoids certificate mismatch with ppa.lau
nchpad.net)
# Debian: uses packages.sury.org and Sury key
